title: My First Weeks in MDS
text:
The First Week of Classes
The first week was fast-paced and more intensive than I expected. We began working with R, Python, statistics, command-line tools, and collaborative workflows. I was especially surprised by how quickly the courses moved from basic concepts to practical exercises. Although I already had experience in AI engineering, the program introduced me to a more systematic way of working with data and communicating analytical results.

title: My First Weeks in MDS
text:
Looking Ahead
I am currently adjusting to the workload and learning how to manage several short assignments at the same time. The pace can be challenging, but I am becoming more comfortable with it. Over the coming months, I hope to strengthen my foundations in statistics and machine learning while connecting them with my previous experience building AI agents. I also look forward to exploring Vancouver and getting to know my classmates better.

title: About
text:
I studied English as an undergraduate and later completed a master’s degree in Linguistics at the University of Wisconsin–Madison. During my graduate studies, I became increasingly interested in natural language processing, machine learning, and software development.
Before coming to Vancouver, I worked as an AI Agent Engineer Intern at Covestro, where I developed agentic AI applications using LangGraph, AWS Bedrock, MCP, and retrieval-augmented generation. I also worked as an AI/ML Software Engineer Intern at BMW, focusing on AI-assisted automotive testing, CAN bus data processing, and workflow automation.
I am now studying in the Master of Data Science program at the University of British Columbia. I came to Vancouver to strengthen my technical foundation and prepare for a career in AI and software engineering.

title: About
text:
Why Data Science
My background in linguistics first introduced me to the challenge of turning human language into structured information that computers can process. As I explored NLP and large language models, I became more interested in building complete AI systems rather than studying language alone.
I chose the MDSCL program to develop stronger skills in statistics, programming, machine learning, and AI. I am particularly interested in building reliable AI agents that can retrieve information, use external tools, analyze data, and complete multi-step tasks. In the future, I hope to apply data science and AI engineering to practical problems in industry.

title: About
text:
Outside of Data Science
Outside of data science, I enjoy cooking Chinese and Japanese food. Some of my favorite dishes to make are gyudon, mapo tofu, Japanese curry, and tomato and egg stir-fry. I also enjoy exploring Vancouver, trying local restaurants, and discovering new neighborhoods.
I recently moved to Vancouver, so I am still learning about the city and building a new life here. I especially enjoy its mild climate, diverse food, and proximity to both the ocean and the mountains.
